Lessons.Title: Representing Exponential Growth
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: identify growth factor and initial value in y=a·b^t, represent repeated multiplication with a table and graph and interpret both parameters in context, including nonzero a^0=1. Independently authored Edulytiks lesson based on Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 5 Lesson 3, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/3/preparation.html and student tasks https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/3/index.html (CC BY 4.0). Source introduces the formal term growth factor and revisits exponent rules.

Independent fictional cell-culture indicator: starting reading12 units and each equal observation period multiplies it by3, so R(t)=12·3^t for integer t≥0. Values at t0,1,2,3 are12,36,108,324. Parameter12 is initial amount (vertical intercept at t0), factor3 is ratio of successive values; an additive difference is not constant. This is pure modeling data and not a real biological growth claim.
Exponent identities: 3^0=1 so R(0)=12, 3^2×3^3=3^5, and (3^2)^3=3^6. Replacing t by t+1 triples the output for every permitted integer period, whereas adding3 each time does not.

Student task: create a labelled table and graph of integer-step readings, match a graph to a multiplication pattern, explain why b>1 describes growth for positive a and derive a new model for a different starting value. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 for table/graph, expression, growth-factor and initial-value interpretation, and justification of exponent properties.

V13 publisher comparison: U5L3 explicitly features an exponent-law Math Talk, an OPTIONAL zero-exponent reminder, two different microbial exponential contexts and their TWO labelled graphs. The original first-party single-model table was mathematically valid but did not ensure both functions/graphs or the optional status of the review.

V13 independent, fictional equal-step growth models: N(t)=50*2^t and P(t)=20*3^t at integer t=0..4. N values [50,100,200,400,800]; P values [20,60,180,540,1620]. Draw both sets of points on clearly labelled axes and compare: N(2)=200>P(2)=180 but N(3)=400<P(3)=540. Initial values are 50 and20 (y intercepts), growth factors2 and3 (successive ratios), not fixed additions. These numbers do not describe actual microbes.

V13 optional exponent-rule discussion: for any nonzero base a, a^0=1. Check 2^3*2^4=2^7=128 and 2^9/2^2=2^7 when dividing by a nonzero value. Correct the misconception 2^3*2^4=2^12; students explain why adding exponents corresponds to repeated factors. The optional review is not mandatory to mark the core lesson assigned.

KeyConcepts.Title: Initial value a
KeyConcepts.Definition: At t0, a·b^0 equals a when b≠0.

KeyConcepts.Title: Growth factor b
KeyConcepts.Definition: For positive a and b>1, the output is multiplied by b each step.
KeyConcepts.Example: R factor3 triples at each period.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exponent rules
KeyConcepts.Definition: When multiplying equal bases, add exponents; a nonzero base raised to zero equals1.

WorkedExamples.Title: Build growth table
WorkedExamples.Question: Use R(t)=12·3^t for t0–3.
WorkedExamples.Method: Investigate the first-party growth/decay table and independently check differences, ratios, exponents, and context.
Steps: Check every next value is triple its predecessor.

WorkedExamples.Title: Interpret factor and intercept
WorkedExamples.Question: What do12 and3 mean in R(t)=12·3^t?
WorkedExamples.Method: Investigate the first-party growth/decay table and independently check differences, ratios, exponents, and context.
Steps: At t0, exponent value1 so output12.
At each one-period increase, factor3 multiplies the previous output.
The graph starts at (0,12) and rises increasingly fast.

WorkedExamples.Title: Use exponent rule safely
WorkedExamples.Question: Simplify 3^2×3^3 and (3^2)^3.
WorkedExamples.Method: Investigate the first-party growth/decay table and independently check differences, ratios, exponents, and context.
Steps: Power of a power multiplies exponents:3^(2×3)=3^6=729.
These are different operations and values.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating growth factor3 as a $3 additive change

CommonMistakes.Correction: Apply b^0=1 before multiplying by a.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using observed-looking biologic readings as evidence of an experiment
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: This dataset is invented for mathematics.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Label it hypothetical and require real provenance for scientific conclusions.

SummaryPoints: Growth models take form a·b^t with initial a and multiplier b>1.
The independent R(t)=12·3^t triples each step.
Exponent zero and multiplication rules explain table structure.
Teacher reviews graph/model interpretations and not fabricated lab work.

Visuals.Title: First-party growth and decay observation table
Visuals.Description: Original hypothetical values calculated from exact models, not real scientific or financial measurements.
